title: No false premise in the question
statement: Every premise a question's wording takes for granted must be true of the text, because a question can presuppose something the text contradicts.
detail: A quality pass on a Grade 9 unit's knowledge base found a learning question that spoke of one character's refusal to follow another, although in the text he does follow him, for his own ends (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`, line 145). It reworded the question to speak of his claim to follow and marked the case fixed.

evidence.quote: Iago's refusal to 'follow' Othello"": Iago does follow Othello, but for himself. Reworded to ""Iago's claim to 'follow' Othello"". Fixed.
